# Schema Documentation

## Database Collections & Field Types

### 1. `users` (User Collection)
* `_id`: `ObjectId` (Primary Key, auto-generated by MongoDB)
* `email`: `String` (Required, unique index, lowercase, trimmed) — User's unique login identity.
* `password`: `String` (Required, select: false) — Bcrypt password hash.
* `name`: `String` (Required, trimmed) — User's display name.
* `role`: `String` (Required, enum: `['manager', 'member']`, default: `'member'`) — Role controlling RBAC permissions.
* `createdAt`: `Date` (Timestamp of account creation)
* `updatedAt`: `Date` (Timestamp of last record update)

### 2. `projects` (Project Collection)
* `_id`: `ObjectId` (Primary Key)
* `key`: `String` (Required, unique index, uppercase, trimmed, length: 2-10) — Project acronym/prefix (e.g., `BUSY`).
* `name`: `String` (Required, trimmed) — Full project name.
* `description`: `String` (Optional, trimmed) — Scope, goals, or client context.
* `owner`: `ObjectId` (Required, ref: `users`, indexed) — Manager who owns and created the project.
* `members`: `[ObjectId]` (ref: `users`, indexed) — Array of users authorized to work on this project.
* `isArchived`: `Boolean` (Default: `false`, indexed) — Soft-delete archive flag.
* `createdAt`: `Date`
* `updatedAt`: `Date`

### 3. `tasks` (Task Collection)
* `_id`: `ObjectId` (Primary Key)
* `projectId`: `ObjectId` (Required, ref: `projects`, indexed) — Project boundary this task belongs to.
* `title`: `String` (Required, trimmed) — Brief summary of the work item.
* `description`: `String` (Optional, trimmed) — Detailed acceptance criteria and specifications.
* `priority`: `String` (Required, enum: `['low', 'medium', 'high']`, default: `'medium'`, indexed)
* `status`: `String` (Required, enum: `['backlog', 'in_progress', 'in_review', 'done', 'blocked']`, default: `'backlog'`, indexed)
* `preBlockedStatus`: `String` (Optional, enum: `['in_progress', 'in_review', null]`, default: `null`) — Denormalized snapshot of prior state before blocking.
* `dueDate`: `Date` (Optional, default: `null`, indexed) — Scheduled deadline.
* `blockers`: `[ObjectId]` (ref: `tasks`) — Task IDs within the same project that block this task.
* `assignees`: `[ObjectId]` (ref: `users`, indexed) — Users responsible for delivering the task.
* `createdAt`: `Date`
* `updatedAt`: `Date`

### 4. `tasktimelines` (Append-Only Audit History & Comments Collection)
* `_id`: `ObjectId` (Primary Key)
* `taskId`: `ObjectId` (Required, ref: `tasks`, indexed) — Target task being tracked.
* `type`: `String` (Required, enum: `['create', 'field_change', 'assign', 'unassign', 'comment']`, indexed)
* `userId`: `ObjectId` (Required, ref: `users`) — Author or actor responsible for the change.
* `fieldName`: `String` (Optional, default: `null`) — Name of the field modified (`status`, `priority`, `dueDate`, `title`, `description`).
* `oldValue`: `Mixed` (Optional, default: `null`) — Pre-change value.
* `newValue`: `Mixed` (Optional, default: `null`) — Post-change value.
* `commentText`: `String` (Optional, default: `null`) — Text body for comments.
* `createdAt`: `Date` (Default: `Date.now`, immutable, indexed) — Exact timestamp of the event.

### 5. `alertdismissals` (Overdue Alert Dismissals Collection)
* `_id`: `ObjectId` (Primary Key)
* `userId`: `ObjectId` (Required, ref: `users`, indexed) — Assignee who dismissed the alert.
* `taskId`: `ObjectId` (Required, ref: `tasks`, indexed) — Overdue task whose alert was dismissed.
* `associatedDueDate`: `Date` (Required) — Snapshot of `task.dueDate` when dismissal occurred.
* `createdAt`: `Date`
* `updatedAt`: `Date`

---

## Relationships

### One-to-Many (1:N)
* **User ➔ Owned Projects**: One user (manager) owns multiple projects (`Project.owner`).
* **Project ➔ Tasks**: One project contains multiple tasks (`Task.projectId`). Every task belongs to exactly one project.
* **Task ➔ Timeline Events**: One task has a chronological stream of timeline audit records (`TaskTimeline.taskId`).

### Many-to-Many (M:N)
* **Projects ➔ Users (Membership)**: A project has many users (`Project.members`), and a user can participate in multiple projects. Modeled as an array of ObjectIds in `Project.members`.
* **Tasks ➔ Users (Assignments)**: A task can have multiple assignees (`Task.assignees`), and a user can hold multiple tasks across projects. Modeled as an array of ObjectIds in `Task.assignees`.
* **Tasks ➔ Tasks (Blocker Dependencies)**: A task can be blocked by multiple tasks, and one task can block multiple others. Modeled as an array of ObjectIds in `Task.blockers`, constrained strictly to the same project.
* **Users ➔ Overdue Tasks (Alert Dismissals)**: Multiple assigned users can dismiss alerts for multiple tasks independently. Modeled via the `alertdismissals` junction collection.

---

## Database vs. Application Constraints

| Constraint | Enforcement Layer | Implementation Details |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Unique Email** | Database | MongoDB Unique Index on `users.email` |
| **Unique Project Key** | Database | MongoDB Unique Index on `projects.key` |
| **Compound Unique Dismissal** | Database | MongoDB Compound Unique Index on `{ userId: 1, taskId: 1 }` |
| **Timeline Immutability** | Database | Mongoose pre-save and pre-query hooks throwing `IMMUTABLE_RECORD` errors on updates or deletes |
| **Task Ownership Scoping** | Application | `verifyProjectAccess` middleware ensures tasks belong to valid projects |
| **Project Member Assignment** | Application | Task creation & update routes verify `assignees ⊆ project.members` |
| **Same-Project Blockers** | Application | `Task.countDocuments({ _id: { $in: blockers }, projectId }) === blockers.length` |
| **Lifecycle State Machine** | Application | `validateTransition()` enforces legal state jumps and blocker resolution before moving to `Done` |
| **Cascade Unassignment** | Application | `Project.members` removal triggers `Task.updateMany` with `$pull: { assignees: userId }` |
| **HTTP History Guard** | Application | Express router returns `403 Forbidden` on `PUT/DELETE` to comments/timelines for all roles |

---

## Deliberate Denormalization

1. **`Task.preBlockedStatus`**: Stored directly on the task document. When unblocking, the system immediately restores `preBlockedStatus` without scanning historical timeline records.
2. **`AlertDismissal.associatedDueDate`**: Stored directly on the dismissal document. Evaluating whether an alert has become stale due to a due date change requires only a simple date equality comparison, without joining across collections.

---

## What Would Become a Bottleneck at 100x Data?

1. **`tasktimelines` Growth**: Every status change, assignment, and comment produces an append-only document. At 100x volume (e.g., 500,000 tasks), this collection will reach millions of rows.
   * *Remedy*: Implement MongoDB collection sharding on `taskId`, and archive historical records of closed projects into cold storage (e.g., S3/Parquet).
2. **Dashboard In-Memory Aggregations**: The `/api/dashboard` route computes headline counts and 8-week completion trends dynamically.
   * *Remedy*: Introduce a materialized summary collection or Redis cache updated incrementally via background jobs.
3. **Regex Text Search**: `GET /api/tasks?search=...` uses case-insensitive regular expressions (`$regex`).
   * *Remedy*: Migrate to MongoDB Atlas Search (Lucene index) or Elasticsearch to avoid unindexed table scans.
